notes: Reference values for calibration harness. Replace with measured commercial-simulator values when available. Re-baselined 2026-08-27 (4th pass). Every drift from the 3rd-pass (2026-08-14) values was attributed by bisect to a deliberate physics correction; none was an unexplained regression. (a) 5f2a4f7 'CFL-adaptive thermal timestep with recalescence cap' caps recalescence at T_sol so a voxel that crosses below solidus on a coarse step is not re-heated into the mushy zone as a permanent hot lump. That moved baseline cast_shrinkage_mean 0.069935 -> 0.083056, baseline side_solidification_time_mean 199.8 -> 163.68, chill side_solidification_time_mean 85.132 -> 74.904, and dual_riser cast_porosity_mean 0.050078 -> 0.0713. (b) 9049ae0 'Fix false shrinkage/porosity risk on chill faces' moved chill_block side_porosity_mean 0.033671 -> 0.017029 (-52%) and chill_block cast_shrinkage_mean 0.034 -> 0.025197, which is precisely that commit's stated purpose. Targets below are the current measured values; tolerances cover run-to-run variance. CORRECTION to the 3rd-pass note: the 'trimesh SIGTRAP flake in core/voxel_mesh.py' was neither trimesh, nor voxel_mesh, nor a flake. It was a deterministic out-of-bounds write in core/feeding_path.py trace_paths_from_risers_batch, which re-pushed already-queued nodes onto a fixed-capacity (n_voxels) frontier on every distance relaxation; under @jit(nopython=True) that unchecked write corrupted the heap and surfaced later as SIGTRAP/SIGSEGV inside libsystem_malloc during unrelated numpy allocation. Fixed 2026-08-27 by relaxing in place instead of re-inserting. Verified result-neutral: dual_riser cast_porosity_mean is 0.072525 both before and after the fix. Re-baselined 2026-10-05 (5th pass) for the gravity-drained riser pipe (physics/riser_pipe.py), which replaced a fixed geometric pipe template. (a) dual_riser cast_shrinkage_mean 0.018729 -> 0.035765: the two 1 in cube risers freeze at 290 s against the casting's 292 s, so the volume balance correctly sends 0.30 in^3 of pipe into the casting; the template had hidden the undersized feeders. (b) riser_post post_porosity_to_riser_ratio 0.466395 -> 0.25836: the pipe stays 2 in above the riser base and the post carries none of it; riser porosity rises because the pipe is now an open cavity. Re-baselined 2026-10-10 (6th pass). riser_post post_porosity_to_riser_ratio 0.25836 -> 0.8665: the 5th-pass value was never reproduced by the committed code. The same commit (1b1a938) also added FeedingPathAnalyzer.liquid_network_cutoff, which flags the riser post as a pinched-off pocket and raises post_porosity_mean 0.0285 -> 0.0662 (riser_porosity_mean 0.0768 -> 0.0764). With the cutoff disabled the ratio is 0.3712. The riser pipe itself stays in the riser (bottom 2.5 in above the riser base, none in the post). Accepted as the current physics. Re-baselined (7th pass) for the pipe in metal no riser feeds (physics.riser_pipe.label_unfed_pools): baseline_block_2in and chill_block have no riser, so their top now sinks like any liquid region that drains by gravity, and the pipe voxels count as shrinkage. baseline_block_2in cast_shrinkage_mean 0.083056 -> 0.117021, chill_block cast_shrinkage_mean 0.025197 -> 0.060199 (the block's feed demand left as open pipe). The other metrics stay inside their tolerances. Re-baselined (8th pass, 2026-11-11) for the insulating sleeve that cuts its riser off from the sand (MoldParams.riser_sleeve_adiabatic = 1, owner: the mold and the cores must not change how fast a riser freezes). On the sand boundary these risers now carry no condition, so they stay liquid while the casting freezes and feed it longer. riser_post_block post_porosity_to_riser_ratio 0.8665 -> 0.372468 (the riser, last to freeze, holds more of the porosity); dual_riser_block cast_shrinkage_mean 0.035765 -> 0.014768. The other metrics stay inside their tolerances. riser_sleeve_adiabatic = 0 gives the 7th-pass values back.
